milestones.title: Klee 1966 / Klee--Walkup 1967 — Hirsch holds for $d \le 3$
milestones.milestone_description: The base of the ladder: in ambient dimension at most three the Hirsch bound $n-d$ holds. Dimensions $0$ and $1$ are near-trivial and force the walk machinery of `DiamLE` to be exercised; dimension $3$ is Klee's exact result $\lfloor 2n/3\rfloor - 1$, weakened to $n-3$. A natural first milestone and the proving ground for the model's definitions.

milestones.title: Larman 1970 — diameter at most $n\,2^{d-3}$
milestones.milestone_description: The classical bound linear in $n$ for fixed $d$, by induction on dimension along a facet decomposition of paths. Incomparable with Kalai--Kleitman: better for small $d$, worse for large. Its induction is a template for every later bound in the ladder.

milestones.title: Naddef 1989 — $0/1$-polytopes satisfy Hirsch
milestones.milestone_description: A one-page argument: projecting onto a coordinate where two vertices differ and inducting. The class covers the polytopes of combinatorial optimization (matching, TSP, stable set). Independent of the rest of the ladder and a self-contained early target.

milestones.title: Kalai--Kleitman 1992 — the quasi-polynomial bound
milestones.milestone_description: The summit of the upper-bound ladder: $n^{\log_2 d + 2}$, proved in under a page by recursing on the polytope's facets and doubling the reachable-facet count. The argument uses almost nothing about geometry — which is exactly why formalizing it cleanly matters: the same induction should apply verbatim to any abstraction satisfying its two axioms.

milestones.title: Todd 2014 — sharpening to $(n-d)^{\log_2 d}$
milestones.milestone_description: The refinement of Kalai--Kleitman by a more careful recursion, later tightened further by Sukegawa. Sits directly above `kalai_kleitman_bound`: the same induction with a better bookkeeping of the base cases. Best done after that milestone falls.

milestones.title: Santos 2012 — a bounded polytope beating $n - d$
milestones.milestone_description: The disproof of the classical conjecture, as an existence statement: exhibit a bounded H-polytope and two vertices with no short path. Unlike the upper-bound ladder this is a finite computation about one explicit object — the 20-dimensional, 40-facet Matschke--Santos--Weibel polytope is the recommended witness — and it is what forces the mission's goal to be the polynomial version rather than $n-d$.
